summary: Short turn that turned the open sweep gap into a buildable case specification instead of activity. The investigation's discriminator now states concretely how the wider event set will be produced: configuration events inject ConfChangeV2 proposals on the current leader (learner add/remove, voter add/remove, a two-change JointImplicit transition with a zero-change follow-up to leave it) and - unlike the previous case, which only advanced raftLog.applied - the harness applies committed conf-change entries through applyConfChange, including the documented rejection form that zeroes NodeId, before advancing the applied index; restart events re-create a node from a MemoryStorage holding its persisted entries and hard state plus a ConfState the harness passes explicitly (CreateSnapshot's cs parameter or an ApplySnapshot carrying it), justified by the premise established last turn that MemoryStorage never tracks configuration; and a liveness witness is recorded for whether any voter can still campaign and be elected, and whether a leader remains, whenever a majority holds a committed-but-unapplied conf change. Its discriminators are the four existing violation events plus a new one for a restarted node whose configuration or committed index contradicts its persisted state, and the summary event will report how many configuration and restart events actually ran; absence over the fixed seed set remains a holds-only result. The knowledge reference for the restart premise was attached, and no experiment was requested because the case is specified but not built - requesting an isolated run of uncompiled harness bytes would risk spending an execution on a harness that does not run. Still open: building and locally compiling that case, and then the gap question about whether the guard's applied-lag condition can leave a cluster without an electable voter in the wider event set.
